newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to upgrade rolling stock with EBRD loan.
newsitem.headline: Romania to upgrade rolling stock with EBRD loan.

text.p: Romania's railway authority will spend $72 million to upgrade its rolling stock over the next year, Transport Minister Traian Basescu said on Thursday.
The funds for the project would come from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Basescu told a news conference.
"We will start the project in January," Basescu said.

Basescu, who took up his duties in the new centrist government last week, also said he was determined to raise passenger fares and freight tariffs to reduce huge losses suffered by the state SNCFR railway authority in recent years.
The upgrading plan included modernisation of both engines and passenger carriages.
He said talks with the local Electroputere Craiova SA locomotive manufacturer and Astra Vagoane rolling stock maker on their participation in the project were in progress.
SNCFR sources said an acute shortage of funds had forced the railway to cut drastically purchases of new rolling stock. Old engines and worn-out carriages are a common sight.
Basescu said low fares and tarrifs enforced by the former leftist government ousted in November parliamentary elections were the main reason for the SNCFR's mounting losses.

"This year alone, the SNCFR has losses amounting to 600 billion lei and there is more to come," Basescu said. "It's incorrect and very harmful for the SNCFR to maintain the present fares under real costs."
The planned tarrifs would fully cover costs related to railway transport. A five percent share of the new tarrifs would be channeled to a new SNCFR development fund, he said.
